# minimaxflash-2 — a Gnome Mage on seed 41

**Depth 1. Character level 1. 158 asks, 1163 keypresses, turn 8001. Ended alive
and well: 8/8 hit points, 1/2 spell points, the game stopped and saved.**

The character was given, not drawn: race `gnome`, class `mage`. The record
compares what the game produced with what was asked, so `born_as_asked` is
`true` for both.

## What happened

I bought a mage's kit in the town (oil, armour, two scrolls of Phase Door,
two potions of Cure Light Wounds), walked down the town's staircase to depth 1,
and then spent the rest of the run trying to find depth 1's down staircase with
the one spell that can find it. It did not work out. The character killed two
monsters (a white icky thing and a soldier ant), learned one spell
(Find Traps, Doors & Stairs), cast it eleven times, and never saw a `>` on the
map.

The interesting part is not the depth. It is that **the mage's staircase hunt is
a 150-ask job and every earlier report in this repository treats it as a
20-ask one**, because nobody had measured the spell's window or its mana
cost.

## The measurements

### The town has a down staircase, and you start on it

`src/gen-cave.c` `town_gen_layout()` ends with:

```c
/* Clear previous contents, add down stairs */
square_set_feat(c, pgrid, FEAT_MORE);
/* Place the player */
player_place(c, p, pgrid);
```

So the town of Angband 4.2.6 has a down staircase on the north wall and the
player is placed **on** it: the status line reads `Down staircase` before you
have pressed anything, and `>` goes straight to depth 1. That is one fewer
staircase hunt than every other run in this repository has assumed.
(`manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` lists ways down and does not mention it; I read the
source at ask 7, after the status line had already told me.)

### The mage's spell finds the staircase, but only in an 81×45 window

`Find Traps, Doors & Stairs` is `DETECT_TRAPS`, `DETECT_DOORS`, `DETECT_STAIRS`,
each with `effect-yx:22:40`. `src/effect-handler-general.c:1467`
(`effect_handler_DETECT_STAIRS`) scans the **real** grid, not the remembered
map, and calls `square_memorize()` + `square_light_spot()` on every stair
square in the window, so it reveals the down staircase even if the character
has never seen it. That is the mage's answer to the hunt that cost
`minimaxflash-1.3` 174 screens.

Two things about it are not in any manual:

1. **The window is 45 rows by 81 columns** (`player->grid.y ± 22`,
   `player->grid.x ± 40`). The level is the full 198×66 — `classic_gen()` does
   `cave_new(z_info->dungeon_hgt, z_info->dungeon_wid)` — so one cast covers
   about 28% of the level. Covering the level takes 3 positions in x and 2 in y,
   i.e. **six casts**.
2. **The spell only reports what it has not already reported.** Cast it twice
   within ten tiles and the second cast says *You sense no traps. You sense no
   doors.* It scans unscanned ground. The mage has to *move* between casts or
   the spell is worth nothing.

And a third, smaller thing: when there is no staircase in the window the
spell says **nothing at all** about stairs. `effect_handler_DETECT_STAIRS` only
prints "You sense no stairs." when `context->aware` is set, and the first
detection never has it. Silence is what "no staircase here" looks like; I
spent several asks wondering whether the effect had failed.

### The mana is the wall, not the stairs

`SP 2/2` at character level 1, and `player_regen_mana()` gives
`msp × 197 + 524` in 65536ths per player action — **0.014 spell points per
action**, so one spell point costs about **71 actions**, and the Find Stairs
spell costs one. Resting doubles it (`percent *= 2`), so one `R` asks fills the
bar again in about 50 actions.

So the arithmetic of the hunt is: six casts × 71 actions = **430 actions of
travel**, plus six asks for the casts and the rests. At the four tiles per ask
this run managed, that is about 150 asks before the staircase is even
*found*. The prompt says "about 150 decisions". **The mage's staircase hunt
consumes the entire budget, and that is the finding.**

### Where the down staircase is

`src/gen-util.c` `alloc_stairs()` picks a random empty floor square with
**exactly three adjacent walls** (a dead-end corridor), relaxing to two, one
and zero walls only if the level has none. `src/gen-cave.c`
`handle_level_stairs()` sets `minsep = MIN(width, height) / 4 = 16`, so the
down staircase is more than 16 tiles from the up staircase in x or y. It is not
in a "staircase room": the up staircase is, the down staircase is just a dead
end.

### AC is the best money a mage can spend

I bought 200 gold of armour — Soft Leather Armour (AC 8, 104), Metal Cap
(AC 3, 24), Leather Shield (AC 8, 66), Cloak (AC 1, 6) — which took the
character from AC 1 to **AC 21**. `src/player-attack.c:196` (`hit_chance`) is

```
hit% = 12% + 83% × (to_hit − 2·AC/3) / to_hit
```

so at AC 21 a monster needs **to-hit ≥ 14** to touch the mage at all, and most
of depth 1 does not. For eight hit points that is the difference between one
fight and five.

### The mage's own weapon is the flask of oil, not the spell

The rapier is useless: to-hit 9 against AC 24 needs to-hit > 16, so melee
lands only on the 12% floor. A flask of oil (9–36, about 22) killed a white
icky thing (6 HP, AC 8) and a soldier ant (AC 4) with one throw each, and the
throw prompt has its own letters: the oil is `a` in the throw list and `c` in
the pack.

## The decisions I would take back

1. **I bought armour before I had measured the stairs.** 200 gold of armour
   was worth it, but the shopping order should have been: oil, armour, **one**
   Phase Door, one Cure Light Wounds, and keep the rest. With 8 hit points the
   escape ladder is worth more than the second potion.
2. **I spent ~30 asks learning how to move.** I did not know that `lxg`
   (look, jump to the nearest unexplored square, walk) is the explorer and that
   aiming the cursor at a *known* landmark gives a 31-step walk. I wrote a
   screen parser to route me around the town map and then used single steps.
   The parser was worth it in the town (four shops, six walks) and useless in
   the dungeon.
3. **I did not spend the rest of the budget on the southern half of the
   level.** The window is 45 rows tall and I was at row ~10, so rows 32–66 were
   never scanned. One cast from y≈40 would have covered more unscanned level
   than the six casts I actually made, all of which were within 40 tiles of
   the first one.
4. **I cast the spell eleven times from inside the same 40-tile band.** The
   spell only reports new squares, so nine of those casts were worth nothing.
   The tell was in the message: "You sense no traps. You sense no doors."
5. **I ate nothing and rested with `R*` without clearing the field.** The rest
   prompt is pre-filled with `& `, so `R*` typed `& *` and rested until
   *healed*, not until spell points were full. One backspace (`src/ui-input.c`:
   "if this is the first time round, backspace means 'delete all'") turns it
   into `R`+BACKSPACE+`*`+Enter, which is the one-ask full rest I used
   afterwards.

## Where the manual was wrong, or not enough

* `manuals/INSTRUCTIONS.md` §8 lists three ways down and does not say that the
  **town** has one, or that you start standing on it.
* The Mage block says "oil (your real attack)" and is right; it does not say
  that the mage's *melee* is nearly worthless (to-hit 9), that its spell
  points regenerate at 0.014 per action, or that Find Traps/Doors & Stairs is
  a staircase detector with an 81×45 window.
* "An unknown potion or scroll pays experience the first time it is used" is
  true but the amount is the *kind's* level, and the Find Stairs spell paid 2
  experience at CL1 — a sixth of the 12 needed for CL2, for a single cast.
* The store mechanics are right in outline and wrong in detail: a purchase is
  `p`, the row letter, the quantity, Enter **and then another key** (the
  Enter is eaten by the quantity prompt), and **when an item sells out the
  whole list renumbers**, so every letter below it changes. I read the letter
  off the screen after every purchase and still got it wrong once.
* Nothing in the repository's documentation says the game can be left sitting
  in the look/targeting mode. It can, and it eats the next several keys. The
  tell is `Press '?' for help.` at the bottom of the screen.

## What I could not see or do

* **I could not see my absolute position on the level.** The map panel scrolls
  and the full map (`M`) draws only the *remembered* region, so after 158 asks
  I still did not know whether I was at x = 20 or x = 120. Without that, the
  six casts I made were aimed at a guess. This is the single thing that made
  the hunt fail: not the spell, not the mana, the arithmetic of where to
  stand.
* **I could not kill anything with AC 24.** A giant black ant (AC 24) or a
  small kobold (AC 24) is unhittable for this character: the oil needs to-hit
  > 2·AC/3 = 16 and the mage's throw is 11. Every fight I won was against a
  low-armour monster, by luck of what walked into my line of sight.
* **I never found a Scroll of Deep Descent**, which `object.txt` gives
  `alloc:20:1 to 100` — that is, a 20% chance on any scroll, findable from
  depth 1 — and which drops you five levels below your deepest. One of those
  would have made the run a depth-6 run. I saw exactly two item glyphs in
  158 asks ('!' a potion and '}' hmm) and never reached them.
* **I could not identify what the 'i' glyph on the floor was** until I read
  `monster_base.txt`: 'i' is the *icky thing* base, a monster, not an item.
  Item glyphs are '!', '?', '(', '=', '"', '_', '\', '|'; letter glyphs are
  monsters. In this game almost everything on the floor is a monster.

## Leads

1. **The mage's hunt is 6 casts at 3 x-positions and 2 y-positions of a
   198×66 level, and each spell point costs 71 actions.** *Evidence:* the
   spell's `effect-yx:22:40` and `alloc_stairs`; `player_regen_mana()`'s
   `msp × 197 + 524`; my eleven casts from inside a 40-tile band. *What would
   settle it:* a run that (a) finds its absolute position — by counting
   tiles walked from the town's staircase, or by using the level's 66-row
   height to calibrate — and (b) casts at exactly (x=40, y=20), (x=120, y=20),
   (x=180, y=20), (x=180, y=45), (x=110, y=45), (x=40, y=45), and reports
   which cast found the `>`.
2. **Can the mage do it in fewer than six casts?** The staircase must be a
   dead end with exactly three adjacent walls, and dead ends are next to
   walls — maybe a `Find Traps` window shows enough structure to aim the next
   cast. *Evidence:* the 11 doors the spell revealed in one window, which is a
   map of the local structure. *What would settle it:* a run that uses the
   revealed doors to choose the next cast's position instead of a fixed grid.
3. **Is the town really the best place to spend 330 gold?** A mage with 8 hit
   points, AC 21, 18 flasks of oil, one Phase Door and one Cure Light Wounds
   may be *too* careful to level: it needs 12 experience for CL2 and only
   low-armour monsters are killable, so it may starve for experience while
   the level's monsters are unhittable. *Evidence:* 4 experience in 158 asks.
   *What would settle it:* a mage run that deliberately buys Magic Missile
   knowledge instead of armour — but it needs CL2 to learn it, and CL2 needs
   experience, and experience needs a killable monster. That circularity is
   worth writing down on its own.
4. **The 'Aim a wand' command swallowed my cast.** After any movement command,
   the key that follows can be read as `a` = "Aim a wand", which then asks
   for a direction and eats everything after it. *Evidence:* asks 91, 92, 98,
   127, 131, 137 of this run — the same "Direction or <click> (Escape to
   cancel)?" prompt five times, always after a walk or a path. *What would
   settle it:* whether `*`+digits+`g` also swallows the next key (it does),
   so that the rule is simply "never send two commands in one ask after a
   movement command".

## The run, in one paragraph

A Gnome Mage with 8 hit points and 2 spell points bought 200 gold of armour
to reach AC 21, learned Find Traps Doors & Stairs, walked down the staircase
that the town puts you on without telling anyone, and then spent the rest of
the run casting a spell that can see a staircase through 81 tiles of dungeon
from a 198-tile-wide level, with one spell point per 71 actions, without
knowing where on the level it was standing. It killed two monsters and
stopped alive at full hit points. The next mage should do three things
differently: buy less armour, learn where it is, and cast the spell six
times from six chosen places instead of eleven times from one.
